title: Subsets II
prompt:
Given an integer array `nums` that may contain duplicates, return all possible subsets (the power set). The solution set must not contain duplicate subsets.

For deterministic comparison, sort each inner subset in ascending order, and sort the outer list of subsets lexicographically.

examples.explanation: Sorting nums first ([1,2,2]) and only branching past the first duplicate at each recursion level prevents [2] or [2,2] from being generated twice.
With both elements equal, the duplicate-skipping rule collapses what would be 4 naive subsets down to just 3 distinct ones.

hints: This is Subsets but with duplicate values in the input — the naive include/exclude backtracking from Subsets will now generate the same subset multiple times.
Sort nums first so that equal values become adjacent, which makes duplicates easy to detect.

At each recursive level, when deciding what to include next, skip a candidate if it equals the previous candidate AT THE SAME RECURSION LEVEL (i.e. you already explored 'include this value' at this position and moved on without it) — this prevents generating the same subset via a different order of picking equal elements.

solution.approach: Sort nums so duplicate values become adjacent. Backtrack with a forward-only start index just like Subsets, recording every partial path as a valid subset. The key fix for duplicates: at each recursion level, when looping over candidate indices from start to end, skip an index if nums[i] == nums[i-1] AND i > start — meaning we already tried including this same value at this level and are now trying to skip it, so trying it again would just reproduce a subset generated by the first branch. This confines duplicate suppression to same-level siblings while still allowing equal values to appear together within a single path (e.g. [2,2]).
solution.code:
def subsets_with_dup(nums):
    nums = sorted(nums)
    result = []
    path = []

    def backtrack(start):
        result.append(path[:])
        for i in range(start, len(nums)):
            if i > start and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]:
                continue
            path.append(nums[i])
            backtrack(i + 1)
            path.pop()

    backtrack(0)
    result.sort()
    return result
